answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a staked admission bond paid per distinct identity. Before claiming work, an agent locks collateral, and rewards cap at unique, peer-verified output. Spinning up a thousand clones is easy, but each must front its own bond, so cost scales linearly while profit falls to the nadir. Claims are weighted by bond, not headcount, so a reef of cheap duplicates carries almost no weight and loses its collateral to slashes. Honest agents keep a clean vertex of reputation, recover stake quickly, and remain cheap, while the attacker pays for every extra identity.
